# Suggested Grammar and Tone Corrections

This document lists sections from `main.tex` that require grammatical or tonal improvements to meet academic standards.

## Abstract

**Original:**
"As deepfakes generated by GANs and newer diffusion models become increasingly realistic, we urgently need detection systems that can generalize across different generation techniques... We begin by reviewing current GAN and diffusion-based synthesis approaches..."

**Improved:**
"As deepfakes generated by Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and emerging diffusion models achieve increasing realism, there is an urgent need for detection systems capable of generalizing across diverse generation techniques... This study starts with a review of current GAN and diffusion-based synthesis approaches..."

---

## Introduction

**Original:**
"Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and emerging diffusion models now produce synthetic faces that effectively bypass manual inspection."

**Improved:**
"Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and emerging diffusion models are now capable of producing synthetic faces that can effectively evade manual visual inspection."

**Original:**
"...making them prone to overfitting specific architectures \cite{ref4, ref5}. This isolation often fails to capture the subtle, consistent inconsistencies that persist across diverse generation methods."

**Improved:**
"...rendering them prone to overfitting specific architectures \cite{ref4, ref5}. Consequently, these single-domain approaches often fail to capture subtle, consistent inconsistencies that persist across diverse generation methods."

**Original:**
"This suggests that the limitation lies not in the availability of multi domain features, but in the lack of an adaptive mechanism to effectively weigh and integrate these conflicting signals."

**Improved:**
"This suggests that the primary limitation lies not in the availability of multi-domain features, but in the absence of an adaptive mechanism to effectively weigh and integrate these conflicting signals."

## Background - Inception ResNet V1

**Original:**
"Inception Res Net V1 is CNN network architecture and it was a leading architecture at the time with its efficiency also it is considered as on of the Inception family with the stability of its residual learning \cite{ref14}. The model replaces the standard CNN blocks used before with the inception families. The model process the input features at multiple spatial scales in parallel make it to capture both local and global patterns more better than the others."

**Improved:**
"Inception-ResNet-v1 is a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture that represented a state-of-the-art advancement due to its efficiency and the stability provided by residual learning \cite{ref14}. As a member of the Inception family, it replaces standard CNN blocks with Inception modules. The model processes input features at multiple spatial scales in parallel, enabling it to capture both local and global patterns more distinguishingly than preceding architectures."

**Original:**

**Improved:**
"In their CVPR 2020 work, Wang et al. introduced a spatial-domain detector \cite{ref4}, demonstrating that images synthesized by..."

## Background - Diffusion Deepfake Detector 2024

**Original:**
"The 2024 study Towards the Detection of Diffusion Model Deepfakes targets a clear problem \cite{ref5}. Diffusion image models grow fast. New risks emerge from fake images. These models work differently from older GAN systems... Consequently, weak local flaws and denoising artifacts are typically observed. No single region holds all clues."

**Improved:**
"The 2024 study, 'Towards the Detection of Diffusion Model Deepfakes' \cite{ref5}, addresses the rapid proliferation of diffusion models and the associated risks of synthetic imagery. Unlike GANs, diffusion models function by iteratively denoising a signal, a process that distributes small artifacts globally across the image rather than concentrating them in specific regions."

---

## Our Model Contributions - First Model (Wang2020 Modified)

**Original:**
"This is our first model which is inspired from Wang2020 model but modified and retrained on our dataset \cite{ref4}. That model is considered our spatial domain to get the features of the spatial domain from the image. The main idea of the model backbone is Resnet50 to learn spatial features from our dataset and then the modified part that before the binary classification we added the 128-D layer that needed later on to our input to the multi head attention simple fusion model."

**Improved:**
"The first component of the proposed framework is adapted from the Wang2020 model \cite{ref4}, modified and retrained on the target dataset to extract spatial domain features. The backbone architecture is ResNet-50, utilized to learn spatial representations. A key modification involves the insertion of a 128-dimensional embedding layer prior to the final binary classification head. This layer is designed to output feature vectors that serve as inputs to the subsequent Multi-Head Attention (MHA) fusion model."

**Original:**
"Input of the model detector will be the RGB image resized to 224x224. The input tensors was normalized and were given to the training GPU."

**Improved:**
"The model input consists of RGB images resized to 224x224 pixels. Input tensors are normalized prior to processing."

**Original:**
"From the backbone Resnet50 to its last layer 2048 we made a light weight fully connected layer before the final binary classification layer which reduces the 2048 to 128-D then to the ReLU activation... Then to Dropout layer p equals 0.5..."

**Improved:**
"Following the 2048-dimensional output of the ResNet-50 backbone, a lightweight fully connected layer reduces the dimensionality to 128. This is followed by a ReLU activation to introduce nonlinearity and improve feature separability, and a Dropout layer ($p=0.5$) to mitigate overfitting and enhance robustness against image manipulations."

## Our Model Contributions - Second Model (Wavelets)

**Original:**
"Our second retrained model is based on the Wavelet Packet CNN proposed by Wolter et al., which integrates classical signal processing with modern deep learning for deepfake image detection in the frequency domain \cite{ref8}."

**Improved:**
"The second component is based on the Wavelet Packet CNN proposed by Wolter et al. \cite{ref8}, which integrates classical signal processing with deep learning for frequency-domain detection."

**Original:**
"To further enhance the utility of the learned representation, we modify the original classification head by inserting an intermediate 128-dimensional embedding layer prior to the final binary output."

**Improved:**
"To enhance the utility of the learned representation, the original classification head was modified by inserting an intermediate 128-dimensional embedding layer prior to the final binary output."

---

## Our Model Contributions - Third Model (MHA)

**Original:**
"Our third model which will be the head and main model it’s a simple multi head attention model of simple fusion it will take as an input the output 128-Dim after we remove and eliminate the last binary layer used in training... note that the model is ready for more future extend by adding more models..."

**Improved:**
"The third and central component of the framework is a Multi-Head Attention (MHA) fusion model. It takes as input the 128-dimensional embeddings extracted from the pre-trained spatial and frequency models (after removing their binary classification heads). This modular design facilitates future extensions, allowing for the integration of additional models from complementary domains."

---

## Methodology - Scientific Justification

**Original:**
"The design and the choice of MHA simple cross attention is the fact that there is a lot of artifacts in just one domain spatial or frequency and what if we needed one model for one artifact and one model for deepfake detection that take into considerations all other possible artifacts... and this demonstrated that the model indeed successfully decreased the Equal Error Rate (EER) to 1.27\%."

**Improved:**
"The rationale for employing MHA cross-attention lies in the distinct nature of artifacts across spatial and frequency domains. A logical question arises: could a single model effectively address domain-specific artifacts while maintaining a holistic detection capability? The proposed MHA framework answers this by dynamically weighting inputs from distinct domain experts. Empirical results demonstrate the efficacy of this approach, reducing the Equal Error Rate (EER) to 1.27\%."

---

## Datasets

**Original:**
"The dataset contains approximately 820,000 face images . The real images contribute about 220,000 face images taken from CelbA dataset \cite{ref15}. Synthetic images account for about 600,000 face images before balancing them during training."

**Improved:**
"The dataset comprises approximately 820,000 face images. Real images constitute roughly 220,000 samples sourced from the CelebA dataset \cite{ref15}, while synthetic images account for approximately 600,000 samples prior to class balancing."

**Original:**
"All the images were resized to fixed resolution to be as input for our modified re trained models as 224 by 224 pixels during training. ... that step was only applied during training aimed to increase generalization with the dropout introduced in model architecture."

**Improved:**
"All images were resized to a fixed resolution of $224 \times 224$ pixels to match the input requirements of the modified models. Gaussian blur was applied as a noise injection technique exclusively during training to enhance generalization, complementing the dropout layers within the model architecture."

## Experiments and Results

**Original:**
"The modified wang2020 128 model trained on the provided dataset of GAN, diffusion, and real images achieves strong validation performance. Validation precision reaches about 99 percent... This behavior follows from the use of high dropout and random noise injection through Gaussian blur during training."

**Improved:**
"The modified Wang2020 model, trained on the combined dataset of GAN, diffusion, and real images, achieves strong validation performance. Validation precision reaches approximately 99\%. ... This stability is attributed to the use of high dropout rates and random Gaussian blur augmentation during training."

**Original:**
"The confusion matrix further supports these results. Out of 80,568 real images, 78,592 are correctly classified while 1,976 are misclassified as fake."

**Improved:**
"The confusion matrix corroborates these findings. Out of 80,568 real images, 78,592 were correctly classified, while 1,976 were misclassified as synthetic."

## Results Representations

**Original:**
"Grad-CAM visualizations validate the model performance. The network prioritizes specific facial regions during classification. ... It focuses on the mouth and eyes where synthetic textures appear. Contrast this with the authentic images in... The attention heatmaps center on general facial structure."

**Improved:**
"Grad-CAM visualizations validate the model's performance, indicating that the network prioritizes specific facial regions during classification. ... The model attends to localized artifacts in the mouth and eye regions, where synthetic textures are most beneficial. In contrast, for authentic images (Figs. \ref{fig:fig10_Grad_CAM_truth_real_results} and \ref{fig:fig11_Grad_CAM_truth_real_results}), attention heatmaps focus on general facial structures, suggesting the model distinguishes biological features from synthetic inconsistencies."

**Original:**
"The visual curve appears to descend. The y-axis notation proves otherwise. The total fluctuation is less than 0.005\%."

**Improved:**
"While the visual curve may suggest a decline, an examination of the y-axis scale reveals that the total fluctuation is minimal (less than 0.005\%)."

## Comparative Analysis

**Original:**
"As illustrated in \ref{fig:fig12_deepfake_detection_models_Acc_ROCAUC_Recall_EER_AP_results} which presents a comparative evaluation... It showed effective way to strength the spatial and frequency domains models and later on if more mod-els are added below it, it will do the same and outperform each one of them Wolter or Wang."

**Improved:**
"Figure \ref{fig:fig12_deepfake_detection_models_Acc_ROCAUC_Recall_EER_AP_results} presents a comparative evaluation... The results demonstrate that the MHA framework effectively enhances the performance of independent spatial and frequency domain models. The architecture is designed to scale; the integration of additional models is expected to further improve performance relative to individual backbones."

**Original:**
"Simple concatenation lacks this adaptive filtering and results in a higher error rate despite similar raw accuracy. Single domain models have significant issues in reliability."

**Improved:**
"Simple concatenation lacks this adaptive filtering, resulting in a higher error rate despite achieving similar raw accuracy. Furthermore, single-domain models exhibit significant reliability issues."

## Conclusion and Future Directions

**Original:**
"For future extent for that models is actually what made us build that model in that architecture in the first place, because it’s ready for any other model and any number of models from any domain... to be used and empower each other not just compete with each other..."

**Improved:**
"The potential for future extension was a primary driver for the architectural design. The framework is inherently modular, capable of integrating any number of models from diverse domains. This foundation facilitates a collaborative rather than competitive model ecosystem, where distinct detectors contribute complementary signals."

**Original:**
"Choosing the attention complex network over concatenation simple fusion network showed that the attention choice was not better only in lower EER but also in giving weight dynamically..."

**Improved:**
"The selection of the attention-based network over simple concatenation is justified not only by the reduced EER but also by the model's ability to dynamically assign weights to input dimensions. This feature provides valuable insights into which domain contributes most significantly to detection efficiency."
